name: Startup Pitch Deck
summary: The investor sequence: problem, solution, market, traction, business model, competition, team and the raise.
references: Guy Kawasaki, The Art of the Start (2004)
Sequoia Capital, Writing a Business Plan guide (2000s)
title_style: Claim titles: one sentence an investor would remember, under 12 words.

sequence.purpose: The painful problem for a clear customer.
The product and its key insight.
Size and shape of the opportunity.
The raise and what it buys.

pitfalls: A market slide with a huge top-down number and no customer logic.
Hiding the ask or leaving out how the money will be used.

example.topic: A fictional agritech startup raising a seed round
outline: Tallyleaf: inventory counts for small farms
Small farms lose a tenth of stock to bad counts
Phone photos turn into accurate counts in seconds
Thousands of small farms in our first region alone
Synthetic pilot: 30 farms, weekly use, zero churn
Monthly subscription per farm, priced by herd size
Clipboards and spreadsheets are the real competitor
A farmer, a vision engineer and a former agri-buyer
Raising a seed round to reach 500 farms
